summary: The note examines the rising cybersecurity threats to telecommunication networks since September 2023, starting with a DDoS attack on major US ISPs and an October phishing campaign. It surveys attack vectors such as malware and ransomware, and defenses including employee training, government regulation, standards compliance, advanced technologies, incident response teams and cyber insurance. It concludes that continuous vigilance and learning from incident reports are needed.
one_line: Overview of telecommunication cyber-attacks since September 2023 and the technical, organizational, regulatory and insurance measures used to prevent and respond to breaches.
key_facts: On September 5, 2023, a cyber-attack on major ISPs disrupted the eastern seaboard of the United States, causing hours of intermittent outages and slowed internet services.
Joanna Shields of TechSecure Inc. described the September 5, 2023 incident as a coordinated DDoS (Distributed Denial of Service) attack and 'a stark reminder of our vulnerabilities.'

On October 21, 2023, a phishing campaign hit thousands of mobile users with texts posing as messages from their carrier, compromising personal data, increasing identity theft and lowering consumer trust.
Michael Anderson, a network engineer, calls ransomware 'the ticking time bomb that can paralyze the whole network once it detonates.'
Adam Thompson, a former hacker turned IT consultant, says attackers look for the weakest link, such as an overlooked software update or a misconfigured firewall.
Melinda Kramer, CIO of GlobalCom, says the focus should be on anticipating attacks, 'not if, but when.'
Recommended resilience measures include multilayered security protocols, regular audits, and AI and machine learning for real-time threat detection.
Jane Fisher, a cybersecurity trainer, says awareness programs and regular drills can make employees 'vigilant gatekeepers rather than unwitting enablers of cyber-attacks.'
After September 2023, the US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) tightened guidelines for telecommunications companies.
The National Cybersecurity Protection Advancement Act is cited as an initiative fostering public-private partnerships for sharing cyber threat intelligence.
ISO/IEC 27001 provides a framework for managing information security; Veronica Lee says compliance 'is not a checkbox exercise; it's a continuous commitment.'
Advanced technologies named include AI-driven behavioral analytics, blockchain for data integrity, and quantum encryption for sensitive data.
Johnathan McKnight says his cyber incidence response team (CIRT) works round the clock and simulates attack scenarios for preparedness.
Cyber insurance policies can cover ransomware, data recovery and legal liabilities.
